review_mode: read-only source, test logic, primary API documentation; no local Windows execution or compilation
disposition: Source review clear after6db+0fe follow-ups; no further concrete blocker found. Actual Windows execution still required.

findings.detail: New readiness verification and outer Job disarm occur after response arrival without the original request deadline, permitting late success.
Creation-failure cleanup has no Job query, so direct wait also needs explicit before/after budget classification.
A new grace clock derived from an earlier parent remaining-time sample could previously accept a late empty Job.
findings.correction: Every before/after Job query uses min(parent.remaining(), grace.remaining()); deterministic control rejects expired parent before and during empty query.

findings.detail: Fresh grace start could previously extend the original cleanup deadline before accepting an empty Job.

confirmed_source_properties: CreateJobObjectW is anonymous and close-kill is enabled before a successfully assigned suspended child resumes.
Failure during Job creation, assignment, or resume invokes bounded direct-child cleanup; assignment failures do not permit uncontained execution.
Only the outer readiness handoff disarms close-kill; the supervisor retains the inner Job and its close-kill flag.
Readiness compares validated private state generation, random token, runtime digest, retained supervisor PID and creation marker, then revalidates serving identity.
Complete cleanup observes direct-child termination and Job ActiveProcesses==0; Job accounting checks budget before and after querying.
Natural descendant grace is at most250ms inside the same two-second retirement budget; forced leftovers cannot become a successful normal exit.
Original setup/wait/exit failures and additional cleanup failure classification are retained through runtime marker mapping.
Actual test probes include assignment failure, exit259, normal root with lingering descendant, bypassed-destructor supervisor exit, installed supervisor termination and authenticated resident reuse.
Handoff checks the original request deadline before readiness, after readiness and after disarm; any expiry retains failure and runs bounded cleanup.
Forced cleanup rearms close-kill before requesting Job termination and retains rearm/termination/wait failures.
Direct-child termination observation rejects expiry before or after the wait even when no Job was created.
Windows outer-startup abort appends cleanup failure when either its existing100ms direct/Job cleanup or50ms generation retirement returns an error; POSIX returned reasons are unchanged.
Natural grace queries use both parent and grace budgets, preventing a freshly started grace timer from extending the cleanup budget.
runtime_evidence_limit: This review did not execute a Windows binary or compiler. Source owner reports pinned rustfmt and companion cross-check; those are distinct from actual Windows Job, abrupt-exit and persistence controls. Hosted Windows qualification is still required.
execution_evidence: No reviewer-owned compile/runtime tests were executed during this source review. Source owner separately reports pinnedRust1.88 formatting and Windows companion cross-compilation; neither is presented here as actual Windows runtime execution.
follow_up_properties: Readiness uses the caller overall_deadline before proof, after proof and after outer close-kill disarm; expired handoff always enters bounded cleanup.
Forced cleanup attempts to rearm close-kill before Job termination, retaining rearm/termination errors and still attempting direct-child cleanup.
Direct child observation requires positive remaining budget before and after the wait, including the no-Job creation-failure path.
Natural grace polling uses min(parent remaining, grace remaining) before and after the Job query and when choosing sleep.

Outer startup abort retains its existing100ms child cleanup and50ms generation cleanup budgets and appends the Windows cleanup-failed marker when either reports failure; POSIX retains its original reason.
